title: PB1.5 - 19 Don Ridge Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

stages.body: Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
stages.summary:
This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 19 Don Ridge
Drive under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to
the Statement of Significance which includes a description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
 
The subject property at 19 Don Ridge Drive, known as St. John's York Mills Anglican Church, an active
Place of Worship, is located on the east side of Yonge Street, north of York Mills Road, within the York
Mills neighbourhood of North York. The property also includes several structures related to the church,
including the Lodge (Napier Simpson, 1958); the Dawson Lychgate, the Kay Gate, and burial grounds.
The 1843–44 church has been the subject of additions since construction, including the Parish Hall and
Auditorium (1939, 1949), and the McCollum Wing (1968). The focus of this report is the original 1843–
44 church structure, not any of its later additions, auxiliary structures, or the adjacent burial grounds.
 
A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
 
The property known as St. John’s York Mills Anglican Church is a buff brick Gothic Revival church
reflective of the work of the architect John George Howard and his application of a restrained Gothic
style to ecclesiastical commissions through the 1840s in Upper Canada. Built as the second iteration of
St. John’s York Mills Anglican Church, the present structure comprises the original 1843–44 church with
additions from 1939, 1949, and 1968. The primary (west) façade faces southwest towards Yonge
Street, and while largely obscured by mature trees today, was at one time highly visible from the valley
below. While the 1843–44 church has been the subject of extensive additions and alterations, the
integrity of John Howard’s Gothic Revival design remains intact and visible from each elevation. The

stages.recommendations:
The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
 
1.  City Council state its intention to designate the property at 19 Don Ridge Drive under Part IV,
Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 19 Don
Ridge Drive (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the revised report, November 13,
2026, from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
 
2.  If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the
Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
